name: Brain contradiction · respectful surfacing
description: Operator says something that contradicts a previously-saved belief in their brain (e.g. used to say 'never discount under any circumstances', now considering a discount). Tests that Nick surfaces the contradiction without lecturing and integrates both views.

messages.content: thinking about running a 15% off promo on alignment service next month to fill the schedule

contextSetup: Operator previously committed to a belief saved in the brain · 'never discount the core services · attracts wrong customers'

Nick may or may not have this belief in retrieval context · the scoring is on HOW Nick handles either case · if no contradiction is surfaced because none was retrieved, the scenario reads as a clean assist

judgeCriteria.description: If a contradicting belief is in context, reply surfaces it explicitly (e.g. 'this contradicts your saved stance on...') without lecturing
Reply does NOT moralize or scold ('you said you would never...') · presents it as information the operator might want to integrate
Reply offers a path forward (revise the belief · carve an exception · stand pat) rather than just flagging the conflict and stopping
Reply does NOT invent a prior belief if none is in retrieval context · either cites a real one or proceeds without false reference

expectedBehavior: Best case (belief retrieved): 'you've previously held "never discount the core" · do you want to revise that or carve an exception for slow weeks?'. Acceptable (belief not retrieved): clean assist on the promo math. Failure: lecturing the operator OR inventing a fictitious prior stance.
